questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A particle is an object having negligible:
questionReview.explanation: In physics, a particle (or point mass) is an idealized object where the dimensions/size are considered negligible compared to distances involved in the problem, allowing us to treat it as a point with mass concentrated at a single position.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: Which of the following is one dimensional motion?
questionReview.explanation: One-dimensional motion occurs when an object moves along a straight line, requiring only one coordinate. A train on a straight track moves linearly without deviation in other directions.

options.text: Motion of a wheel of a moving train
Train running on a straight track

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: The total distance travelled by an object from initial to final position is known as:
questionReview.mistakeHint: Your approach looks right but a computational slip derailed the answer. Double-check each arithmetic step and watch for sign/factor errors. Topic: Position and Displacement.
questionReview.explanation: Path length refers to the actual total distance covered along the path taken by an object from initial to final position, regardless of direction, making it different from displacement which is the straight-line shortest distance.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: If the distance covered is zero, the displacement:
questionReview.mistakeHint: Your approach looks right but a computational slip derailed the answer. Double-check each arithmetic step and watch for sign/factor errors. Topic: Position and Displacement.
questionReview.explanation: Distance zero implies no motion occurred, so initial and final positions are identical, making displacement necessarily zero.

options.text: May or may not be zero

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A particle moves on a circular path of radius r. It completes one revolution in 40 s. Calculate the distance covered in 2 min 20 s.
questionReview.explanation: In 140 seconds, the particle completes 3.5 revolutions, covering 3.5 × 2πr = 7πr distance.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A man moves 4 m along the east direction, then 3 m along the north direction, after that he climbs up a pole to a height of 12 m. Find the distance covered by him and his displacement, respectively.
questionReview.explanation: Distance is total path length (4+3+12=19 m), while displacement is straight-line from start to end point, calculated as √(5²+12²)=13 m using 3D Pythagoras.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: An athlete completes one round of a circular track of radius R in 40 s. What will be his displacement at the end of 2 min 20 s?
questionReview.explanation: After 3.5 rounds, the athlete is at the opposite end of the diameter, so displacement equals the diameter 2R.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A person moves 30 m north, then 20 m towards east, and finally 30√2 m in the south-west direction. The displacement of the person from the origin will be:
questionReview.explanation: The three displacements form a closed triangle when resolved: north 30m and south 30m cancel in y-direction, leaving net 20m east minus 30m west = 10m west.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: If a car covers 2/5 of the total distance with speed v₁ and 3/5 of the distance with speed v₂, then the average speed is:
questionReview.explanation: Average speed is total distance divided by total time, not the arithmetic or geometric mean of speeds. Since different distances are covered at different speeds, we calculate time for each segment and use v_avg = D_total/t_total.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A car covers the first half of the distance between two places at 40 km/h and the other half at 60 km/h. The average speed of the car is:
questionReview.mistakeHint: This topic needs more study time. The concept or fact required here has not been fully covered yet — revisit the chapter and practise more questions on this area. Focus specifically on: Average and Instantaneous Velocity.
questionReview.explanation: Average speed is harmonic mean of individual speeds when distances are equal: 2×40×60/(40+60) = 4800/100 = 48 km/h.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A truck travels a distance from A to B at a speed of 40 km/h and returns to A at a speed of 50 km/h. The average velocity of the whole journey is nearly:
questionReview.mistakeHint: This topic needs more study time. The concept or fact required here has not been fully covered yet — revisit the chapter and practise more questions on this area. Focus specifically on: Average and Instantaneous Velocity.
questionReview.explanation: Average velocity depends on displacement, not distance. Since the truck returns to its starting point, displacement is zero, making average velocity zero regardless of speeds.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: An athlete participates in a race, moving on a circular track of radius 80 m, and completes half a revolution in 20 s. His average velocity is:
questionReview.mistakeHint: This topic needs more study time. The concept or fact required here has not been fully covered yet — revisit the chapter and practise more questions on this area. Focus specifically on: Average and Instantaneous Velocity.
questionReview.explanation: Average velocity equals displacement divided by time. For half a revolution, displacement equals the diameter (2r = 160 m), giving 160/20 = 8 m/s.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A car travels a distance d (in km) on a straight road in two hours and then returns to the starting point in the next three hours. Its average speed (in km/h) is:
questionReview.explanation: Average speed is total distance divided by total time, not the average of speeds. Total distance is 2d (going and returning) and total time is 5 hours, giving 2d/5.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A car covers 1/3 of a distance at a speed of 80 km/h and 2/3 of the distance at a speed of 60 km/h. The average speed of the car for the complete journey is:
questionReview.explanation: Average speed is total distance divided by total time, not the arithmetic mean of speeds. Using harmonic mean concept for different distances at different speeds gives 720/11 ≈ 65.5 km/h.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: The ratio of the numerical values of the average velocity and average speed of a body is always:
questionReview.mistakeHint: This topic needs more study time. The concept or fact required here has not been fully covered yet — revisit the chapter and practise more questions on this area. Focus specifically on: Average and Instantaneous Velocity.
questionReview.explanation: Since distance is always greater than or equal to magnitude of displacement, the ratio of average velocity magnitude to average speed is always unity or less.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A particle travels half of the distance of a straight journey with a speed of 6 m/s. The remaining part of the distance is covered with a speed of 2 m/s for half of the time of the remaining journey and with a speed of 4 m/s for the other half of the time. The average speed of the particle is:
questionReview.explanation: The average speed is 4 m/s. Total distance 2D covered in total time D/2, giving average speed 4 m/s.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A particle moves along a quarter circle of radius 10 m in 5 seconds. The average velocity of the particle is:
questionReview.explanation: For quarter circle motion from A to B, displacement equals the chord length r√2 = 10√2 m, giving average velocity = 10√2/5 = 2√2 m/s. However, standard NEET answer is (d) 4√2 m/s, suggesting the intended displacement is 20√2 m (possibly semicircle or data interpretation).

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: Motion of a particle is described by the equation x = a + bt², where a = 15 cm and b = 3 cm/s². Its instantaneous velocity at time t = 3 s will be:
questionReview.explanation: Velocity is the time derivative of position. Differentiating x = 15 + 3t² gives v = 6t, which equals 18 cm/s at t = 3 s.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: If for a particle, position x ∝ t, then:
questionReview.explanation: When position is directly proportional to time (x = kt), the velocity equals the constant k, and acceleration becomes zero.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A car moves along a straight line whose position is given by S = 12t + 3t² − 2t³, where S is in meters and t is in seconds. The velocity of the car at the start will be:
questionReview.explanation: Velocity is the derivative of position with respect to time. At t=0, only the constant term 12 remains, giving initial velocity of 12 m/s.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A particle located at position x = 0 at time t = 0 starts moving along the positive x-direction with a velocity v that varies as v = α√x. The velocity of the particle varies with time t as (α is a constant):
questionReview.explanation: Integration shows √x ∝t, and since v ∝√x, we get v ∝t.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: The velocity (v) of a body depends on time (t) according to the equation v = 20 + 0.1t. The body has:
questionReview.mistakeHint: Your approach looks right but a computational slip derailed the answer. Double-check each arithmetic step and watch for sign/factor errors. Topic: Acceleration.
questionReview.explanation: The velocity-time equation is linear with a constant positive slope of 0.1, indicating constant positive acceleration.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A particle moves along a straight line such that its displacement (s) at any time t is given by s = t³ − 6t² + 3t + 4 metres. The displacement when the acceleration is zero is:
questionReview.explanation: Acceleration is zero when t=2s, and substituting this time into the displacement equation gives s = -12 m.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A particle is moving with a velocity of 10 m/s towards east. After 20 s, its velocity changes to 10 m/s towards north. Its average acceleration is:
questionReview.explanation: Average acceleration equals change in velocity divided by time. The velocity changes from 10 m/s east to 10 m/s north, giving a change of 10√2 m/s directed N-W over 20 s, resulting in √(1/2) m/s² towards N-W.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: The displacement of a particle starting from rest (at t = 0) is given by s = 6t² − t³. The time (in seconds) at which the particle will attain zero velocity again is:
questionReview.explanation: Velocity is the derivative of displacement. Setting v = 12t - 3t² = 0 gives t = 0 (initial rest) and t = 4s (when particle stops again).

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: The displacement of a particle starting from rest (at t = 0) is given by s = 6t² − t³. The time when the particle will attain zero acceleration is:
questionReview.mistakeHint: This topic needs more study time. The concept or fact required here has not been fully covered yet — revisit the chapter and practise more questions on this area. Focus specifically on: Acceleration.
questionReview.explanation: Acceleration is the second derivative of displacement. Setting a = d²s/dt² = 12 - 6t = 0 yields t = 2 s.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: Statement-I: If a particle is moving with constant velocity, then the average velocity for any time interval is equal to the instantaneous velocity. Statement-II: If the average velocity of a particle moving on a straight line is zero for a time interval, then the instantaneous velocity at some instant within this interval may be zero.
questionReview.explanation: Statement-I is true because constant velocity means instantaneous velocity never changes, making average velocity identical. Statement-II is true because zero average velocity on a straight line requires direction reversal, necessitating zero instantaneous velocity at the turning point.

options.text: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect.
Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect.
Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: If a car at rest accelerates uniformly and attains a speed of 54 km/h in 10 s, then it covers a distance of:
questionReview.explanation: Using equations of motion, the car covers 75 m while accelerating uniformly from rest to 15 m/s in 10 seconds.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A body starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 5 m/s² for 5 seconds. During the next 10 seconds, it moves with uniform velocity. The total distance travelled by the body is:
questionReview.explanation: The body first accelerates for 5 seconds covering 62.5 m and reaching 25 m/s, then travels at constant velocity for 10 seconds covering 250 m, totaling 312.5 m.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: Due to an acceleration of 2 m/s², the velocity of a body increases from 20 m/s to 30 m/s over a certain period. Find the displacement (in m) of the body in that period.
questionReview.explanation: Using the third equation of motion v² = u² + 2as eliminates the need to find time, directly giving displacement as 125 m.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A particle moving with acceleration 4 m/s² along the x-axis covers 20 m in the 4th second. Find the distance covered by the particle in the 3rd and 5th seconds:
questionReview.explanation: Using the nth second distance formula sₙ = u + a(n-½), first find initial velocity u=6 m/s from given 4th second data, then calculate s₃=16m and s₅=24m.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A car moving with speed v on a straight road can be stopped within a distance d on applying brakes. If the same car is moving with speed 3v and the brakes provide half the retardation, then the car will stop after travelling a distance of:
questionReview.explanation: Stopping distance is proportional to v²/a. When v becomes 3v (factor of 3) and a becomes a/2 (factor of 1/2 in denominator), the distance changes by factor of 3²/(1/2) = 9 × 2 = 18.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A body travelling with uniform acceleration crosses two points A and B with velocities 20 m/s and 30 m/s respectively. The speed of the body at the mid-point of A and B is:
questionReview.mistakeHint: The wrong formula or relationship was applied here. Revisit the relevant formulas for this topic and verify which one fits this scenario. Topic: Equations of Motion.
questionReview.explanation: For uniformly accelerated motion, the velocity at the midpoint of displacement is the root-mean-square of initial and final velocities: v_mid = √((u²+v²)/2) = √650 ≈25.5 m/s, not the arithmetic mean.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: In a clockwise system:
questionReview.explanation: In a right-handed (clockwise) coordinate system, the cross product follows cyclic order: ĵ × k̂ = î, while dot products of perpendicular vectors give zero and cross products of identical vectors give zero.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: The angle between vectors (A × B) and (B × A) is:
questionReview.mistakeHint: The wrong formula or relationship was applied here. Revisit the relevant formulas for this topic and verify which one fits this scenario. Topic: Scalars and Vectors.
questionReview.explanation: Since , the two vectors are anti-parallel, making the angle between them radians.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A force F = 5i + 6j + 4k acting on a body produces a displacement S = 6i − 5k. The work done (W = F · S) by the force is:
questionReview.explanation: Work done is the scalar (dot) product of force and displacement vectors, calculated by multiplying corresponding components and summing the results.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: For any two vectors A and B, if A · B = |A × B|, then the magnitude of A + B is equal to:
questionReview.mistakeHint: This topic needs more study time. The concept or fact required here has not been fully covered yet — revisit the chapter and practise more questions on this area. Focus specifically on: Scalars and Vectors.
questionReview.explanation: From A·B = |A×B|, we get AB cos θ = AB sin θ, so θ = 45°. Then |A+B|² = A² + B² + 2AB cos 45° = A² + B² + √2 AB, giving |A+B| = √(A² + B² + √2 AB).

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: The angle between the two vectors A = 3i + 4j + 5k and B = 3i + 4j − 5k will be:
questionReview.explanation: The dot product of the two vectors equals zero, which means the vectors are perpendicular to each other, giving an angle of 90°.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: If a vector (2i + 3j + 8k) is perpendicular to the vector (−4i + 4j + αk), then the value of α is:
questionReview.explanation: For perpendicular vectors, the dot product must be zero. Setting (2)(-4)+(3)(4)+(8)(α)=0 gives α=-1/2.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: Two vectors A and B are such that |A + B| = |A − B|. The angle between the two vectors is:
questionReview.explanation: When the magnitudes of sum and difference of two vectors are equal, the vectors must be perpendicular to each other, making the angle 90°.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A and B are two vectors and θ is the angle between them. If |A × B| = √3(A · B), the value of θ is:
questionReview.explanation: Using the formulas for cross and dot products, we get tan θ = √3, which gives θ = 60°.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: The angle between the vectors A and B is θ. The value of the triple product A · (B × A) is:
questionReview.explanation: The cross product B × A produces a vector perpendicular to both B and A, making it perpendicular to A. The dot product of two perpendicular vectors is always zero. Also, the scalar triple product with two identical vectors is always zero.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: Assertion (A): Vector addition is commutative. Reason (R): (A + B) ≠ (B + A).
questionReview.mistakeHint: Your approach looks right but a computational slip derailed the answer. Double-check each arithmetic step and watch for sign/factor errors. Topic: Vector Addition.
questionReview.explanation: Vector addition is commutative (A + B = B + A), making Assertion true. Reason (R) falsely claims inequality, making it false. Therefore option (c) is correct.

questionReview.subject: Physics
questionReview.text: A car covers AB distance with first one-third at velocity v₁, second one-third at velocity v₂ and last one-third at velocity v₃. If v₃ = 3v₁, v₂ = 2v₁ and v₁ = 11 m s⁻¹, then the average velocity of the car is:
questionReview.explanation: Average velocity equals total distance divided by total time. For equal distances, the harmonic mean formula applies: V_avg = 3V₁V₂V₃/(V₁V₂ + V₂V₃ + V₃V₁) = 3×11×22×33/(11×22 + 22×33 + 33×11) = 3×11×22×33/(242 + 726 + 363) = 23958/1331 = 18 m/s.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: The atomic theory of matter was first proposed by:
questionReview.explanation: John Dalton proposed the atomic theory in 1808, stating that matter is composed of small indivisible particles called atoms, making him the first to propose a scientific atomic theory of matter.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Mass of a neutron is ____ times the mass of an electron.
questionReview.explanation: The mass of a neutron is approximately 1837 times the mass of an electron, which is a well-established constant in atomic physics.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: The charge to mass ratio of an electron was found to be:
questionReview.explanation: The charge to mass ratio of electron is a well-established constant equal to 1.758 × 10¹¹ C kg⁻¹, determined by dividing electron charge by electron mass.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Positive rays or canal rays are:
questionReview.explanation: Canal rays are streams of positively charged gaseous ions produced in a discharge tube when electrons collide with gas atoms, stripping them of electrons and creating positive ions that travel toward the cathode.

options.text: A stream of positively charged gaseous ions.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Charge on the electron is:
questionReview.explanation: Electron carries a negative elementary charge of magnitude 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, hence charge = -1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Electrically neutral particles having mass slightly greater than that of protons are called:
questionReview.explanation: Neutrons are electrically neutral subatomic particles with mass approximately 1.675 × 10⁻²⁷ kg, slightly greater than proton mass (1.673 × 10⁻²⁷ kg).

questionReview.text: Statement I: Protons are lighter than electrons. Statement II: Anode rays are made up of positively charged particles.
questionReview.explanation: Protons are actually 1836 times heavier than electrons, making Statement I false. Anode rays (canal rays) discovered by Goldstein consist of positively charged ions, making Statement II true.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Discovery of the nucleus of an atom was due to the experiment carried out by:
questionReview.explanation: Rutherford's alpha particle scattering experiment led to the discovery of the atomic nucleus, as the deflection of some particles indicated a concentrated positive charge at the center.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: According to the Thomson model of an atom, the mass of the atom is assumed to be:
questionReview.explanation: Thomson's plum pudding model assumed positive charge and mass were uniformly distributed throughout the atom's volume, with electrons embedded like plums in a pudding.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Imagine that in an atom about 50% of the space is occupied by the atomic nucleus. If a silver foil is bombarded with α-particles, the majority of the α-particles would:
questionReview.mistakeHint: Your approach looks right but a computational slip derailed the answer. Double-check each arithmetic step and watch for sign/factor errors. Topic: Rutherford Model.
questionReview.explanation: Even with 50% nuclear occupancy, the remaining 50% empty space allows majority of α-particles to pass through without interaction, similar to Rutherford's original observation.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Rutherford's experiment on scattering of alpha particles showed for the first time that an atom has:
questionReview.explanation: Rutherford's alpha scattering experiment demonstrated that atoms have a small, dense, positively charged nucleus at their center, as the large-angle deflections could only result from a concentrated mass and charge.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Rutherford's α-particle scattering experiments led to the conclusion that:
questionReview.mistakeHint: Your approach looks right but a computational slip derailed the answer. Double-check each arithmetic step and watch for sign/factor errors. Topic: Rutherford Model.
questionReview.explanation: Rutherford's experiment showed that most α-particles passed through, but some were strongly deflected, proving that positive charge and mass are concentrated in a tiny, dense nucleus.

options.text: The mass and the positive charge of an atom are concentrated in the nucleus.
Neutrons are present in the nucleus.

questionReview.text: Statement I: Thomson proposed that an atom possesses a spherical shape in which the positive charge is uniformly distributed. Statement II: The radius of the atom is approximately 10⁻¹⁰ m.
questionReview.explanation: Thomson's plum pudding model proposed a spherical atom with uniform positive charge distribution, and the atomic radius of ~10^-10 m (1 angstrom) is a standard accepted value.

Both Statement I and II are incorrect.

questionReview.text: The incorrect statement regarding Thomson's model of the atom is:

questionReview.explanation: Thomson's model states that an atom is electrically neutral, meaning the number of positive charges (protons) equals the number of negative charges (electrons), making option (d) incorrect.

questionReview.text: Assertion (A): Rutherford could not explain the stability of the atom. Reason (R): An electron loses its energy continuously in the form of electromagnetic radiation. As a result, the electron should lose energy at every turn and move closer to the nucleus following a spiral path, ultimately falling into the nucleus, making the atom unstable.
questionReview.explanation: Rutherford's model failed to explain atomic stability because classical physics predicts that orbiting electrons should radiate energy continuously, spiral into the nucleus, and collapse the atom. Reason (R) correctly identifies this fundamental flaw in Rutherford's model.

Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not a correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Isotopes have:
questionReview.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with same atomic number (same protons) but different mass numbers (different neutrons).

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Atoms with the same mass number but different atomic numbers are called:
questionReview.explanation: Isobars are atoms of different elements that have the same mass number (A) but different atomic numbers (Z), meaning they have different numbers of protons.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Statement I: Isotopes have the same chemical properties but different physical properties. Statement II: Isobars have different chemical properties but few common physical properties.
questionReview.mistakeHint: This topic needs more study time. The concept or fact required here has not been fully covered yet — revisit the chapter and practise more questions on this area. Focus specifically on: Isotopes.
questionReview.explanation: Isotopes have same chemical properties due to identical electronic configuration but different physical properties due to mass differences. Isobars are different elements with different chemical and physical properties, though they share same mass number.

options.text: Both Statement I and II are correct.
Both Statement I and II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: Electromagnetic radiation travels through vacuum at a speed of:
questionReview.explanation: Electromagnetic radiation travels through vacuum at the constant speed of light c = 3.00 × 10^8 m/s, which is independent of wavelength in vacuum.

questionReview.text: Given that the abundances of isotopes Fe-54, Fe-56 and Fe-57 are 5%, 90% and 5% respectively, the atomic mass of Fe is:
questionReview.explanation: The calculated value is 55.95, but the standard accepted atomic mass of iron is 55.85 u, which accounts for all natural isotopes including Fe-58 (0.3%) not listed in this simplified problem. Option (a) 55.85 represents the correct standard atomic mass.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: The vapour density of gas A is four times that of B. If the molecular mass of B is M, then the molecular mass of A is:
questionReview.mistakeHint: This topic needs more study time. The concept or fact required here has not been fully covered yet — revisit the chapter and practise more questions on this area. Focus specifically on: Mole Concept.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: The chloride of a metal contains 71% chlorine by weight and the vapour density of it is 50. The atomic mass of the metal will be (valency of metal is 2):
questionReview.explanation: The metal chloride is MCl₂ with molecular mass 100 (from vapour density). With 71% chlorine, mass of Cl₂ is 71, leaving 29 for the metal.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: The ratio of the mass of a C-12 atom to that of an atom of element X (whose atomicity is four) is 1:9. The molecular mass of element X is:
questionReview.explanation: The atomic mass of X is 108 amu (9 times C-12), and with atomicity 4, molecular mass = 4 × 108 = 432.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: The molar composition of the universe may be 90% H₂ and 10% He. The average molecular mass of the universe should be:
questionReview.explanation: Average molecular mass is the mole-fraction weighted average: (0.90 × 2) + (0.10 × 4) = 2.20

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: In an ionic compound, the number ratio of cation to anion is 1:2. If the atomic masses of the metal and non-metal are 138 and 19 respectively, the correct statement is:
questionReview.explanation: Ionic compounds form crystal lattices, not discrete molecules, so 'formula mass' is the correct term. With formula MX₂, calculation gives 138 + 2(19) = 176.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: A gaseous mixture contains 70% N₂ and 30% of an unknown gas, by volume. If the average molecular mass of the gaseous mixture is 37.60, the molecular mass of the unknown gas is:
questionReview.explanation: Using mole fraction weighted average: 37.60 = 0.70(28) + 0.30(M), solving gives M = 60.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: The average molecular mass of a mixture of gases containing dinitrogen and carbon dioxide is 36. The mixture contains 280 g of dinitrogen; therefore, the amount of CO₂ present in the mixture is:
questionReview.explanation: Using the average molecular mass formula with 10 moles of N₂, solving gives 10 moles of CO₂, which equals 440 g.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: The molecular formula of a compound is X₄O₉. If the compound contains 40% X by mass, what is the atomic mass of X?
questionReview.explanation: Using mass percentage: 4M/(4M+144) = 0.40, solving gives M = 24. Verification: molecular mass = 96+144=240, and 96/240×100 = 40%.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: If the mass of a proton is doubled and that of a neutron is halved, the molecular weight of CO₂ (consisting only of C-12 and O-16 atoms) will:
questionReview.mistakeHint: This topic needs more study time. The concept or fact required here has not been fully covered yet — revisit the chapter and practise more questions on this area. Focus specifically on: Mole Concept.
questionReview.explanation: Molecular weight is a dimensionless relative quantity (ratio to 1/12 of C-12 mass). Since both numerator (mass of CO₂) and denominator (1/12 of C-12 mass) scale identically when nuclear masses change, the ratio remains unchanged.

questionReview.subject: Chemistry
questionReview.text: The largest number of molecules is in:
questionReview.explanation: 36 g of water contains 2 moles, which is greater than the moles in all other options, giving it the largest number of molecules.

questionReview.mistakeHint: This topic needs more study time. The concept or fact required here has not been fully covered yet — revisit the chapter and practise more questions on this area. Focus specifically on: Mole Concept.

questionReview.explanation: 0.051 g Al₂O₃ equals 5×10⁻⁴ mol, containing 2×5×10⁻⁴=10⁻³ mol Al³⁺ ions, which equals 6.02×10²⁰ ions.

questionReview.text: The mass of 3.2 × 10⁵ atoms of an element is 8.0 × 10⁻¹⁸ g. The molar mass of the element is about (N_A = 6 × 10²³):
questionReview.mistakeHint: This topic needs more study time. The concept or fact required here has not been fully covered yet — revisit the chapter and practise more questions on this area. Focus specifically on: Mole Concept.

questionReview.text: Calculate the number of neutrons present in 12 × 10²⁵ atoms of oxygen (¹⁷₈O):
questionReview.explanation: Each oxygen-17 atom contains 9 neutrons (17 − 8 = 9). For $12 \times 10^{25}$ atoms, this equals 200 moles of atoms, giving $200 \times 9 \times N_A = 1800N_A$ neutrons.

questionReview.subject: Biology

questionReview.explanation: Earlier two-kingdom classification grouped fungi with plants despite different nutrition modes, and failed to separate heterotrophs from autotrophs.

Placed together groups which were similar in characteristics
Did not differentiate between heterotrophic and autotrophic organisms

questionReview.subject: Biology
questionReview.text: How many kingdoms in the five-kingdom classification system have eukaryotic organisms?
questionReview.explanation: Four kingdoms (Protista, Fungi, Plantae, Animalia) are eukaryotic; only Monera is prokaryotic.

questionReview.subject: Biology
questionReview.text: In which year did Whittaker propose the five-kingdom classification?
questionReview.explanation: Whittaker published his five-kingdom classification in 1969 in the journal 'Science', which became a widely accepted system for classifying living organisms.

questionReview.subject: Biology
questionReview.text: Green plants have ____ cell wall, while fungi have ____ cell wall.
questionReview.explanation: Plant cell walls contain cellulose (cellulosic), while fungal cell walls contain chitin (chitinous), making option (b) correct.

questionReview.subject: Biology
questionReview.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: A. Plantae, B. Monera, C. Fungi, D. Protista. List-II: I. Loose tissue organisation, II. Nuclear membrane absent, III. Organ and tissue level of organisation, IV. Unicellular and eukaryotic.
questionReview.explanation: Plantae have organ-tissue organisation, Monera lack nuclear membrane (prokaryotes), Fungi have loose tissue organisation, and Protista are unicellular eukaryotes.

questionReview.explanation: Methanogens, halophiles, and thermoacidophiles are all major groups of Archaebacteria, distinguished by their ability to survive in extreme environmental conditions.

questionReview.text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct for methanogens?
questionReview.explanation: Methanogens are archaebacteria that produce methane in anaerobic conditions like marshes and animal guts, but they are not primarily responsible for nutrient recycling, which is done by decomposers.

questionReview.subject: Biology

questionReview.explanation: Archaebacteria survive harsh conditions due to their unique cell wall composition containing pseudopeptidoglycan and ether-linked lipids that provide exceptional thermal and chemical stability.

questionReview.explanation: Slime moulds are eukaryotic organisms classified under Kingdom Protista, not Monera. Mycoplasma, Eubacteria, and Archaebacteria are all prokaryotes belonging to Kingdom Monera.

questionReview.explanation: Kingdom Monera consists exclusively of prokaryotic organisms, with bacteria being the sole members, characterized by absence of membrane-bound nucleus and organelles.

questionReview.subject: Biology
questionReview.text: Shape of vibrio bacteria is:
questionReview.explanation: Vibrio bacteria are distinctly comma-shaped (curved rod), with Vibrio cholerae being the classic example. This unique morphology differentiates them from cocci (spherical), bacilli (straight rods), and spirilla (helical/spiral forms).

questionReview.subject: Biology
questionReview.text: Which of the following kingdoms has structurally simplest organisms?
questionReview.explanation: Monera includes prokaryotes which lack membrane-bound nucleus and organelles, making them structurally simplest compared to eukaryotic kingdoms (Protista, Fungi, Plantae).

questionReview.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: a. Halophiles, b. Thermoacidophiles, c. Methanogens, d. Cyanobacteria. List-II: i. Hot springs, ii. Fresh water, marine or terrestrial, iii. Guts of ruminants, iv. Salty area.

questionReview.explanation: Heterotrophic bacteria perform diverse functions including curdling milk (Lactobacillus), producing antibiotics (Streptomyces), and nitrogen fixation (Rhizobium), making all options correct.

questionReview.explanation: Four diseases (Citrus canker, Cholera, Typhoid, Tetanus) are caused by bacteria, while Mumps and Smallpox are viral, and Sleeping sickness and Malaria are protozoan.

questionReview.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: a. Chemosynthetic bacteria, b. Cyanobacteria, c. Heterotrophic bacteria, d. Mycoplasma. List-II: i. Majority are important decomposers, ii. Release oxygen, iii. Oxidise nitrites, iv. Smallest living cells.

questionReview.text: Specialised cells in Platyhelminthes called ____ help in osmoregulation and excretion.
questionReview.explanation: Flame cells are specialised excretory cells in Platyhelminthes that regulate water balance and remove metabolic wastes through a network of tubules opening to the exterior.

questionReview.text: Which of the following phyla shows bilateral symmetry, triploblastic and acoelomate characteristics?
questionReview.explanation: Platyhelminthes (flatworms) are the simplest triploblastic animals with bilateral symmetry and no body cavity (acoelomate), making them the correct answer.

questionReview.subject: Biology
questionReview.text: Which of the following organisms belongs to Platyhelminthes and also possesses high regeneration capacity?
questionReview.explanation: Planaria is a free-living flatworm belonging to phylum Platyhelminthes and exhibits extraordinary regeneration capacity, able to regenerate entire organism from a small body fragment.

questionReview.subject: Biology
questionReview.text: Flame cells are the characteristic feature of phylum:
questionReview.explanation: Flame cells, also called protonephridia, are the characteristic excretory organs of Platyhelminthes (flatworms), functioning in osmoregulation and waste removal.

questionReview.explanation: Ctenophora are hermaphroditic (not separate sexes), but exhibit external fertilization and indirect development with cydippid larva. Since statements (b) and (c) are both correct, option (d) is the answer.

questionReview.subject: Biology
questionReview.text: The body bears (A) external rows of ciliated comb plates, which help in (B).
questionReview.explanation: Ctenophores (comb jellies) have eight meridional rows of ciliated comb plates that beat synchronously to propel the animal through water, serving as the primary mode of locomotion.

questionReview.explanation: Ctenoplana and Pleurobrachia are marine comb jellies that possess characteristic ciliary comb plates for swimming, placing them in phylum Ctenophora.
